deliveryPackage.builtFromDiffNote: The package was built 36 commits before the release commit. Those 36 commits carry all 11 gate fixes landed for this release, so the package does NOT contain them. The package metadata recorded the true commit (a93880e) — the version label was what drifted.
deliveryPackage.productionReadyReason: Native linux/amd64 acceptance steps P0-3 through P0-6 were not executed; the local build host was arm64.

runs.trigger: push to main (head = 14a8bee, the released commit itself)
runs.note: The authoritative gate run for this release: all four Required checks are green here. customer-amd64-native does not apply on a branch ref, so it is skipped in this run and runs in the tag run instead.
The release tag event. customer-amd64-native only executes on a v* tag ref, so this is where it ran - and failed. See that gate entry.

gates.name: customer-amd64-native
gates.reason: Ran on the v2.0.0 tag push: the job condition is startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v'), so it is skipped on branch and main pushes but does execute on a release tag. The candidate image built successfully (sha256:d3a23a66e66220875fdb3d0a4dc632a4ea6a272eaf480878cead3cef1dc81e24, tagged ghcr.io/kaelio/project-lucy:candidate-amd64-2.0.0-20261023-14a8bee) but the push was denied with 'permission_denied: The requested installation does not exist'. Root cause: the workflow logs in to GHCR with this repository's built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, which can only write packages under the repository owner (Forrest219), while the image repository defaults to the kaelio namespace, a different owner. Because the candidate digest never reached the registry, the native amd64 gates and the container-level smoke were skipped, and real-e2e, customer-release-readiness and release-package were skipped downstream. This is the same defect seen on the v0.2.0 tag run 40052825697; review section 4.23.

gates.name: real-e2e
gates.reason: Two independent blockers. First, its upstream customer-amd64-native failed on the tag run, so the job was skipped rather than scheduled. Second, even with that fixed, no self-hosted runner is registered (labels self-hosted, lucy-protected, linux, amd64), so the job stays BLOCKED and never degrades to a headless or local result.

gates.name: customer-release-readiness
gates.reason: Depends on real-e2e and was therefore skipped in both runs. No automated release credential was produced.

gates.name: release-package
gates.reason: Depends on customer-release-readiness and was therefore skipped in both runs, so no GitHub-gate-produced delivery package exists for this release.

gates.name: P0-3 through P0-6
gates.reason: Manual native linux/amd64 acceptance. The local build host was arm64.

gates.name: demo-db-smoke, postgres-demo-db-smoke
gates.reason: Ran and failed for the known deployment-layer reason recorded in review section 4.20: the demo compose files mount no bootstrap token and hard-code a token path that does not exist in a clean checkout. Not one of the four Required checks, so it did not block the release; deferred to the 2.5 line.

notes: The release was merged as a merge commit (242 commits, squash disabled) so the branch head SHA survives verbatim in main history and the commit / image digest / package SHA256 triple stays traceable.
The GitHub Release for this tag carries the full evidence write-up in prose only; it has no attached machine-readable artifacts.

This product version was corrected to 0.2.0 on 2026-10-24 because 2.0.0 was too easily confused with the Helm Chart version line 0.2.x. The v2.0.0 tag and its Release are kept as historical fact and are not deleted or moved.
Root-cause ledger for the 11 gate defects: docs/reviews/2026-10-23-lucy-v2.0-release-readiness-review.md sections 4.8 through 4.20.

A release is verified by more than one CI run, so this entry lists both of them under runs. The push run on the released commit is the authoritative gate run; the tag-push run is where the tag-only gates execute. Every gate cites one of the listed runs.
The customer release chain was already blocked by the candidate image push failure on the tag run, independently of the missing self-hosted runner. Review section 4.23.
